name: steady-weeks
description: Ordinary reflective weeks: a postponed course, a small win, a quiet weekend. The baseline fixture — every persona should produce a schema-valid, grounded letter with zero rubric violations.

entries.body: Monday. I finally enrolled in the typography course I keep postponing. The sign-up took four minutes; I had spent four months dreading it. What does that say about the difference between a task and the story I tell myself about the task?
Midweek note: the first lesson was on whitespace. 'The page is not empty because it is quiet.' I kept thinking about that all day, mostly while sitting in meetings that had too many words in them.

Sunday. Walked the long way home on purpose. No headphones for once. I noticed I reach for my phone whenever there is a gap in stimulation, like the gap is a problem to solve instead of the actual point.
I told my brother about the course. He asked what I wanted it to become — a job, a hobby, a proof of something. I didn't have an answer and that felt honest rather than evasive, for once.
